observations: Photo 0 shows a black laptop open, displaying a desktop with a blue and purple abstract wallpaper. The screen has a visible MSI logo on the bezel. The keyboard is backlit with green lighting on the right edge. The laptop is placed on a white surface, with a store interior in the background, including a green-lit wall and a sign that says 'GEEK CONSULT NG'.

Photo 1 shows the same laptop from a side angle, with the screen partially closed. The left side of the laptop is visible, showing ports including USB and HDMI. The MSI logo is visible on the lid. The background is consistent with photo 0, indicating the same location.
The laptop appears to be a gaming model, with a thick chassis and visible cooling vents on the side.
The screen bezel is thick, especially on the top and sides, typical of older gaming laptops.
No visible damage to the exterior in either photo.
The seller claims it is an MSI GE66 Raider 11UG with an Intel Core i7-11800H processor, but no model label or sticker is visible in the photos to confirm this.

claims.evidence: The MSI logo is visible in photo 0 and photo 1, but no model name or sticker is visible to confirm the GE66 Raider 11UG model. The seller's text is not proof.
Processor specifications cannot be verified from photos. The laptop is powered on in photo 0, but no system information is visible on screen. No BIOS or system info screen is shown.
Origin and condition cannot be verified from photos. The laptop appears clean, but 'fresh' and 'UK used' are not provable remotely.

risks.proof: A screenshot of the system information (e.g., Windows System Info or CPU-Z) showing the exact CPU model and specifications.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic 11th gen laptop, not as a high-end i7-11800H model

risks.risk: Laptop may have hidden physical damage or screen issues not visible in photos
risks.proof: A video showing the laptop being opened, closed, and rotated, with close-ups of the screen for dead pixels or backlight issues, and the hinges for wear.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having potential screen or hinge issues

risks.risk: Battery may be degraded or non-functional
risks.proof: A video showing the laptop running on battery power for at least 5 minutes, with battery percentage visible.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if battery is not working

risks.risk: Laptop may have been refurbished or have replaced parts
risks.proof: A photo of the bottom panel showing the serial number and any service stickers, or a screenshot of the BIOS showing the model and serial number.
